articleTitle: A Study on Cognitive Effects of Canvas Size for Augmenting Drawing Skill
abstract: In recent years, the field of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in the domain of image generation, has exerted a profound influence on society. Despite the capability of AI to produce images of high quality, the augmentation of users' drawing abilities through the provision of drawing support systems emerges as a challenging issue. In this study, we propose that a cognitive factor-specifically, the size of the canvas-may exert a considerable influence on the outcomes of imitative drawing sketches when utilizing reference images. To investigate this hypothesis, a web-based drawing interface was utilized, designed specifically to evaluate the effect of the canvas size's proportionality to the reference image on the fidelity of the drawings produced. The findings from our research lend credence to the hypothesis that a drawing interface, featuring a canvas whose dimensions closely match those of the reference image, markedly improves the precision of user-generated sketches.

articleTitle: Kimono Fashion Development Based on the Fusion of Digital Art and Digital Textile Printing
abstract: We have developed Kimono fashion by integrating digital art and digital textile printing technology.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality System Supporting Food Culture Learning
abstract: Informal cultural learners will continue to engage in learning as long as the information they receive remains appealing and interesting. They are also the target audience for cultural learning that leads to cultural awareness and preservation. To support food culture learning of informal learners, we propose an immersive experience system focusing on Japanese food culture learning. We designed a visually appealing virtual learning environment, using virtual reality technology to immerse users in diversified cultural scenarios. We also designed and introduced interesting tasks based on these scenarios, providing guidance while enhancing user engagement. Finally, we conducted an experiment to confirm the learning effectiveness and motivation of the participants.

articleTitle: Interactive Design System for Dynamic Comics from Video Sequence
abstract: Dynamic comics are widely used in video production to summarize sequences efficiently but require manual design processes and specialized skills. In this paper, we propose an interactive tool that allows users to convert input videos into dynamic comics. First, the user specifies the segmentation points on the input video. The system then computes the locations of comic panels using a parametric layout model and composites the set of video segments. A user study evaluates the system's effectiveness and gathers feedback on dynamic comic design tools.

articleTitle: TexControl: Sketch-Based Two-Stage Fashion Image Generation Using Diffusion Model
abstract: Deep learning-based sketch-to-clothing image generation provides the initial designs and inspiration in the fashion design processes. However, clothing generation from freehand drawing is challenging due to the sparse and ambiguous information from the drawn sketches. The current generation models may have difficulty generating detailed texture information. In this work, we propose TexControl, a sketch-based fashion generation framework that uses a two-stage pipeline to generate the fashion image corresponding to the sketch input. First, we adopt ControlNet to generate the fashion image from sketch and keep the image outline stable. Then, we use an image-to-image method to optimize the detailed textures of the generated images and obtain the final results. The evaluation results show that TexControl can generate fashion images with high-quality texture as fine-arained Image generation.

articleTitle: Emergent Text-to-Image Generation Using Short Neologism Prompts and Negative Prompts
abstract: When using text-to-image generation models, AI artists often use long prompts to generate desired images. However, this poster proposes a method for generating diverse painterly images using Stable Diffusion and short prompts of only 1–2 words. This method employs neologisms (or coined words) to diversify the generated images and employs negative prompts to drastically transform the images. I found that this not only diversifies the images but also significantly changes the image style.

articleTitle: Facial Animation Retargeting by Unsupervised Learning of Graph Convolutional Networks
abstract: This paper proposes an unsupervised framework for retargeting human facial animations to different characters. Our method uses a branching structure of two parallel auto encoders and a variant of generative adversarial networks. The two au-toencoder branches, composed of graph convolutional networks, share a common latent space through which the retargeting between different mesh structures can be performed. The shared latent codes are obtained by graph pooling operators, and the character face is reconstructed from the latent codes by the unpooling operators. The graph pooling and unpooling operators are designed based on multiple landmarks in optical-based facial motion capture systems. The GAN-based unsupervised learning method requires no paired training animation data between source and target characters. Our experimental results demonstrated that the proposed framework provides a reasonable estimation of a target facial expression that mimics a source character.

articleTitle: Automatic Scenario Generation for Customer Service Training VR System
abstract: Customer service training systems utilizing VR are used as a customer service training method in the service industry, such as restaurants. These systems train according to pre-defined scenarios, which can cause problems, such as people tending to memorize the contents of the scenarios, such as the corresponding locations, and stopping paying attention to their surroundings after repeated training. This paper proposes a system in which the training scenario changes with each experience. The system can generate approximately 230,000 training scenarios by changing the customer service task, the customer's location, the content of the customer service task, and the order in which they occur in the scenario.

articleTitle: Edge Feature Extraction for Shape Similarity Metric of Stone Tool by 3D Measured Point Cloud
abstract: In the realm of archaeological research, the accurate identification and matching of stone tools plays a pivotal role in identifying and reassembling stone tools. Traditional meth-ods of stone tool analysis often rely on manual inspection, a time-consuming and labor-intensive process. The fusion of real-world measurements, edge points extraction, and sophisticated shape similarity evaluation metrics presents a compelling avenue for en-hancing the identification and improving stone tool identification. Some methods, such as selecting a candidate point of feature lines by its Mahalanobis's distance, and the downside of extracting ambiguous ridgelines, hardly extract edge features as intended. In other words, accurate evaluation of surface sharpness is a critical challenge in distinguishing edge points. While traditional thinning methods of point clouds have limitations due to their complexity, the integration of edge features and junction regions enhances the efficiency of feature extraction and expects to simplify the similarity estimation process. Therefore, this paper presents a method of extracting edge features and junction region of edge points for shape similarity metric of stone tools by 3D measured point cloud.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Optimization for Fitting Parameters of Measured Isotropic Spectral BRDFs
abstract: Parametric Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF), which represents the surface reflectance with parametric models, is compact, efficient to render, and easy to edit. The parameters for the parametric BRDFs are often obtained by fitting them with measured surface reflectances of real-world materials at RGB channels. In recent years, the surface reflectances at densely sampled wavelengths, referred to as measured spectral BRDFs, have been publicized. Fitting parametric BRDFs with measured spectral BRDFs is difficult since the number of parameters is prohibitive compared with that for measured RGB BRDFs. This paper proposes a two-stage optimization method to fit the parameters of parametric BRDFs with measured spectral BRDFs. In the first stage, our method fits the wavelength-independent parameter with the average surface reflectance of all discretized wavelengths. Then, the wavelength-dependent parameters are fitted for each discretized wavelength, reducing the number of simultaneously optimized parameters. Experimental results show that our fitting parameters can provide plausible rendering results.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning Pipeline for Hand Image Generation U sing Diffusion Model
abstract: The hand images generated by the image generative model may suffer distortions, such as stable diffusion. To solve this issue, we introduce a hand image fine-tuning pipeline consisting of three stages: hand detection, object masking, and image inpainting. First, a hand detection model is trained to identify flawed hands using bounding boxes (Bbox), Then, these Bbox regions are masked in conjunction with Mediapipe landmarks. Finally, a ControlN et model is trained for inpainting the masked areas, and the targeted LoRA is also trained to minimize bound-ary fragmentation. The results indicate that our method achieves better anatomical accuracy in hand reconstruction compared to the original diffusion model. Furthermore, the introduction of the directional LoRA model further enhances the evaluation outcomes.

articleTitle: Image Enhancement for Dichromats by Weighting the Color Difference Between Neighboring Pixels
abstract: Dichromats recognize colors using two out of three cone cells; L, M, and S. To extend the ability of dichromats to recognize the color difference, we propose a method to expand the color difference when observed by dichromats. We analyze the color between the neighboring pixels in chromaticity space. In order to exaggerate the neighboring pixels as much as possible, we set the initial value randomly for iterative updation. On the other hand, in order to preserve the naturalness of the detailed structure, we weight parameters adequately to the cost function. Our method fully enhances the color difference between different color region so that the dichromats recognizes the color difference between neighboring pixels.

articleTitle: A Study on Impact of Displaying Depth on User Recognition to Virtual Information
abstract: Optical see-through head-mounted display (OST-HMD) presents virtual information as an overlay to the real world. User's capability to recognize the virtual information can be varied according the depth of the virtual information being presented, as well as its distance to user's vergence on a real object. However, there are still no study comprehensively investigate the impact of the displaying depth on user's recognition. In this study, we propose and conduct two experiments to explore how the displaying depth influences a user's capability to recognize information presented by an OST-HMD, and search for the optimal depth for displaying virtual information so that a user can recognize efficiently. A hypothesis can be made that a user's capability to recognize presented information by OST-HMD will be decreased with the displaying depth increasing, or with the increasing of discrepancy between vergence and depth. And this hypothesis was supported by the experimental result.

articleTitle: A Proposal and Experiment of Multi-Colored Switching Animation
abstract: We have devised a multi-colored switching animation and are investigating the method and possibility of its realization. Specifically, we realize an animation by illuminating illustrations drawn in multiple colors with light from stage lighting and switching the light colors. In this study, we have been implementing and experimenting with a basic system for multicolor switching animation.

articleTitle: An Immersive Method for Extracting Structural Information from Unorganized Point Clouds
abstract: Point clouds find extensive applications across diverse domains such as construction, architecture, and archaeology due to their capacity to encapsulate rich datasets. Given the density and detail of these datasets, extracting accurate structural information (geometrical and connectivity information) demands sophisticated algorithms and tools. The recent advancements in virtual reality (VR) technology and rendering techniques have significantly elevated the ability to visualize these point cloud datasets, affording users an immersive experience within the data. This immersive capability holds the potential to streamline the process of extracting valuable information from these datasets. In this work, we explore the feasibility of extracting and visualizing structural information from point clouds with immersive interfaces. We propose strategies to enhance human perception of the underlying structure and interactive methods to extract face, edge, vertex, and connectivity data from the raw, unorganized point clouds. Our method is evaluated based on public datasets. We believe our work represents a promising attempt to integrate human insights into the data processing pipeline.

articleTitle: STMA: A Fast Visual Field Defect Assessment Method Using Quadtree and Head-Mounted Display
abstract: Individuals with eye diseases that cause optic nerve damage, such as glaucoma, suffer from visual field defects (VFDs), rendering the assessment of VFDs an essential step in medical treatment. In existing studies, various methods have been proposed for VFD area inspections. However, these methods present several problems, including long inspection times and the need to maintain a posture for extended periods, potentially placing significant physical and psychological burdens on patients and affecting the accuracy of the inspection result. Moreover, loose eye fixation constraints also decrease the reliability of the result. In response, we herein propose a novel approach for a fast VFD test, facilitated by the quadtree algorithm. To overcome the physical burden caused by posture constraints related to the testing area requirements and location of the stimulus, the proposed VFD test is implemented on a head-mounted display with a built-in eye tracker. To improve the accuracy of the inspection result further, variously sized noise fields were adopted as the stimuli shown to the examinees. In addition, to validate the performance of the proposed method, a mock experiment was conducted in this study, which involved volunteers with normal vision. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method demonstrates a competitive advantage in perimetric time compared to current state-of-the-art methods, and it exhibits advantages in terms of both accuracy and user comfort.

articleTitle: Perceptual Uniformity-Aware Image Recoloring Method for Red-Green Anomalous Trichromacy
abstract: Color vision deficiency (CVD) is one kind of common disability fundamentally caused by genetic disorders, which lowers individuals' capability to distinguish colors and results in a loss of chromatic contrast. Although the state-of-the-art method for CVD compensation has been proposed, which can evenly deal with varying degrees of CVD, it suffers from the limitation of the color space while performs the recoloring, which lacks perceptual uniformity. More-over, its high computational time as well as complex parameter settings hinder its practical use. In this paper, we put forward an image recoloring algorithm for contrast enhancement for CVD compensation in the CIE L*a*b* color space, which can be adapted to the personal degree of CVD. In addition, the proposed algorithm maintains the naturalness of the original image by imposing a constraint on the compensation range. Furthermore, a discrete solver has been introduced to tackle the optimization problem effectively. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, quantitative and subjective experiments have been conducted, and the experimental results show that our method achieved the best scores for contrast enhancement.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Learning Approach for Avatar Action Identification in the Metaverse
abstract: Avatars are vital in the metaverse as they represent users and their interactions within the digital environment. This research delves into understanding and identifying avatar actions in the metaverse to enhance virtual interactions for increased safety and contextual awareness. While avatar actions share similarities with human movements, they also exhibit distinct patterns and levels of freedom. As a result, the study focuses on transferring knowledge from human actions to comprehend avatars' behavior in the metaverse. To improve the interpretation of avatar movements, a model pre-trained on human actions is trained using a small amount of avatar action data. The study compares this “few-shot” model with a “zero-shot” model (which doesn't use any avatar data) and a model exclusively trained on avatar data. The analysis employs the Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) model for handling avatar skeleton data and an MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) model for classifying avatar actions. Ultimately, the study finds that the few-shot model surpasses the zero-shot model in terms of effectiveness and adaptability to avatars. Moreover, in comparison to the model trained solely on avatar data, the few-shot model demonstrates high generalizability and emerges as a robust performer, showcasing its ability to effectively classify actions across various types of avatars.

Message from General and Program Chairs; NICOInt 2024
abstract: Welcome to the Proceedings of the 23rd NICOGRAPH International, which is held from June 14 to 15, 2024 at Tokyo Metropolitan University, Hachioji, Tokyo, Japan. This conference is in cooperation with ADADA JAPAN. NICOGRAPH has a quarter-century of history. Its foundation can be traced back to 1985. The time-honored annual conferences have been organized by the Society for Art and Science (SAS) since 2000, which aim at promoting the research combining science and art in computer graphics and related fields as well as advancing the development of interactive media art. In 2002, the first international conference, NICOGRAPH International, rose out of the domestic series and since then NICOGRAPH International has been organized annually.
